The generalization error bottleneck observed (train_err $\ll$ heldout_err) is not due to insufficient capacity ($N_c$), but rather a "diffusion barrier" in the weight landscape where the optimizer gets trapped in a local minimum that fits the training points but fails to interpolate the held-out region, akin to a metastable state in a glassy energy landscape.

The apparent "fatness" of the solution space is an artifact of the basis function representation; specifically, using a polynomial basis with high dynamic range (as hinted in the failure mode regarding run29) artificially inflates the effective dimensionality of the function space, making a rigid problem appear under-constrained unless the basis is normalized to $O(1)$.
